No perf-critical issues are verifiable in this diff since the actual query engine (go-duck) was removed and replaced with stubs — the main risk is the feature is now a guaranteed failure path gated behind a flag

adjudication_records.issue_text: `enableSqlExpressions` in pkg/expr/reader.go:196-201 computes the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and both branches return false, so the function can never return true and the feature gate is a no-op; intended logic (return the flag value) was inverted/mangled

`TablesList` in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:11-16 now uses the stub sql.NewInMemoryDB whose RunCommands always returns 'not implemented', so this exported function always errors at runtime — a silent behavioral regression for existing callers with no feature-flag protection

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior DuckDB implementation (`duck.NewInMemoryDB()` from `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`) with `NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`. `NewInMemoryDB()` is newly added in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` and returns a `*DB` whose `RunCommands` method always returns `"not implemented"`. Since `TablesList` calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`, `TablesList` will now deterministically error at runtime. There is no feature-flag check inside `TablesList` to prevent this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `SQLCommand.Execute` in pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-102 builds the full execution path (mathexp.Results, frames, logs) against a stub db.QueryFramesInto that unconditionally fails, shipping a permanently-failing execution branch that will break all SQL expression queries once the gate is fixed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `pkg/expr/sql` in-memory DB whose `QueryFramesInto` unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")` (pkg/expr/sql/db.go). `SQLCommand.Execute` is updated to call this stub (`db := sql.NewInMemoryDB(); err := db.QueryFramesInto(...)`), so the execution path would always fail if reached. However, in the same diff `ReadQuery` gates `QueryTypeSQL` via `enableSqlExpressions(h)`, and `enableSqlExpressions` currently returns `false` in all cases, making the SQL execution path unreachable as shown. So it’s not a present, verifiable runtime defect in this PR, but it is a concrete completeness/architecture issue: enabling the flag later would expose an always-failing implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' at pkg/expr/reader.go:131-133 masks the real cause (broken enableSqlExpressions logic) and will waste debugging time on flag configuration (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, QueryTypeSQL now gates execution on enableSqlExpressions(h) and returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when it returns false. But enableSqlExpressions is clearly broken: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both branches, so it will always disable SQL expressions regardless of flag state. This makes the emitted error misleading (implies missing implementation rather than disabled/broken gating) and will hinder debugging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: enableSqlExpressions check is inverted (!IsEnabledGlobally) so feature flag semantics are broken in pkg/expr/reader.go:193-199

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go the new enableSqlExpressions() is incorrect: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (inverting the flag meaning) and then returns `false` in all paths (`if enabled { return false }; return false`). As a result, QueryTypeSQL always errors with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of the feature flag state, breaking intended feature-flag semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: SQL string built via fmt.Sprintf with naive single-quote doubling in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:24-26, a latent SQL injection pattern reachable once the gate is fixed

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList constructs a SQL command via fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) after only doubling single quotes (strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)). This is indeed string-concatenated SQL with ad-hoc escaping, which is a recognizable latent injection/robustness risk pattern. However, the diff also introduces a gate that currently always disables SQL expressions (enableSqlExpressions always returns false) and replaces the DuckDB implementation with a stub DB whose RunCommands returns "not implemented", so an actual exploitable injection/behavioral defect is not verifiably reachable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Removed dependencies still referenced in go.sum/go.work.sum (e.g., hairyhenderson/go-which, iancoleman/orderedmap hashes persist), risking desynchronized resolution across workspace vs module builds

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the cited removed dependencies’ hashes being removed from go.sum: `github.com/hairyhenderson/go-which` and `github.com/iancoleman/orderedmap` entries are explicitly deleted. They also do not appear to persist in go.work.sum in this diff. While go.work.sum gains some entries (e.g., overflow, thrift, asmfmt, minio) and loses others (e.g., azblob, go-replayers), the specific claim that removed deps like go-which/orderedmap remain referenced in sums is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns false in both branches (`if enabled { return false }; return false`), so it unconditionally returns false. ReadQuery’s QueryTypeSQL case now errors whenever `!enabled`, meaning SQL expressions will always return `sqlExpressions is not implemented` regardless of the feature flag state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sql_command.go still allocates the DB and frame per execution even though the call can only fail — wasted work on the hot query path

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go, Execute() still allocates a new in-memory DB (sql.NewInMemoryDB()) and a new data.Frame on each call before invoking db.QueryFramesInto(...). In this diff, pkg/expr/sql/db.go implements QueryFramesInto() as a stub that always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so the call cannot succeed and those allocations/work are currently pointless. This is a concrete inefficiency/cleanup issue introduced by the change, though the claim about it being a “hot query path” isn’t verifiable from the diff (and SQL parsing is also gated to always return an error in reader.go).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-request in-memory DuckDB construction in sql_command.go:96 and parser.go:24 creates a new DB instance per query with no pooling/reuse or cap on concurrent queries, which will cause heavy per-request allocation/GC pressure and unbounded concurrent in-memory databases under load if the real implementation is restored

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a new in-memory DB instance being created per call (`sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` and `NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`), but the newly added implementation is a stub `DB{}` with methods that just return `errors.New("not implemented")` (no DuckDB engine, no allocations/pooling issues are evidenced). Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false`, so `QueryTypeSQL` is hard-disabled in `pkg/expr/reader.go`, making the claimed per-request load/concurrency impact unobservable from this diff. The finding’s “heavy allocation/GC pressure” and “unbounded concurrent in-memory databases under load if the real implementation is restored” is speculative and not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go builds SQL by single-quote-escaped string interpolation into json_serialize_sql('%s'), which is fragile — edge cases like backslashes or dialect differences could break or allow command manipulation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TablesList` still constructs a command via string interpolation: `cmd := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only replacing `'` with `''`. That is indeed a fragile way to embed arbitrary SQL text into another SQL statement (escaping assumptions, edge cases), even though it’s intended to pass the SQL as a string literal. However, the diff does not demonstrate an actual, exploitable injection or broken behavior (and the new in-memory DB stubs currently return `not implemented`), so this is best treated as a robustness/security-hardening review issue rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No perf-critical issues are verifiable in this diff since the actual query engine (go-duck) was removed and replaced with stubs — the main risk is the feature is now a guaranteed failure path gated behind a flag

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes SQL expressions a guaranteed failure path. In `pkg/expr/reader.go`, `enableSqlExpressions()` returns `false` unconditionally (it returns false in both the `if enabled { ... }` branch and at the end), so `ReadQuery` will always return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` for `QueryTypeSQL` regardless of feature flags. Additionally, the removed `go-duck` engine is replaced by `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` stubs where `RunCommands`, `TablesList`, and `QueryFramesInto` all return `"not implemented"`, so even if the gate were fixed the functionality would still error at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: enableSqlExpressions in pkg/expr/reader.go ends with unconditional return false and the flag check is inverted (enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)), so SQL expressions are always rejected even when the feature flag is ON; the gate is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() unconditionally returns false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false in both the `if enabled` branch and the final return. As a result, the new QueryTypeSQL gate (`if !enabled { return ..., fmt.Errorf(...) }`) always rejects SQL expressions even when the feature flag is enabled, making the flag check dead/broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: pkg/expr/sql/db.go and pkg/expr/sql_command.go replace all real DuckDB logic (duck.NewInMemoryDB, QueryFramesInto, RunCommands) with stubs returning 'not implemented', silently breaking all SQL expression queries with no migration note

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the real DuckDB dependency (`github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`) and replaces usage with a new `pkg/expr/sql` DB whose methods `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all return `errors.New("not implemented")` (pkg/expr/sql/db.go). Call sites were updated to use these stubs (e.g., pkg/expr/sql_command.go now calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`, which will always error). Additionally, SQL query reading is now gated by `enableSqlExpressions`, but that function always returns false regardless of flags (pkg/expr/reader.go), causing `ReadQuery` to return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` for `QueryTypeSQL`. This verifiably breaks SQL expression execution compared to the prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' in pkg/expr/reader.go conflates 'flag disabled' with 'not implemented', producing misleading telemetry that makes incidents hard to triage

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the SQL path gates execution on enableSqlExpressions(h); when it returns false (i.e., feature flag not enabled), the code returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). This error string does not reflect the actual condition shown in the diff (feature-gated/disabled vs. truly unimplemented), so the finding about conflating “flag disabled” with “not implemented” is supported by the diff and is an actionable observability/diagnostics issue rather than a core correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go still contains SQL-sanitization code but now always errors because NewInMemoryDB's RunCommands always returns 'not implemented', breaking previously working callers

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now does `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()` and then calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`. The new implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go defines `RunCommands` to always return `"not implemented"`, so TablesList will always fail at runtime. This is a concrete behavior change from the previous `go-duck` backing implementation and would break any callers relying on TablesList.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Dead branch in pkg/expr/reader.go: if enabled { return false } followed by return false means the IsEnabledGlobally result is never used; the PR appears incomplete but merged, with unrelated dependency removal churn mixed in

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the newly added enableSqlExpressions() always returns false: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` but both the `if enabled { return false }` branch and the final `return false` return false. As a result, in ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL the code will always hit `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`, effectively disabling SQL expressions regardless of the feature flag value. This is a verifiable dead/ineffective branch and broken gating behavior introduced by the diff.
